 Missouri revenue department blocked 8,000 fraudulent tax refund claims this year
 Published 4:03 pm Thursday, November 19, 2026
 By STAFF REPORT 
 Missouri Department of Revenue 
 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 JEFFERSON CITY — The Missouri Department of Revenue said it has blocked more than 8,000 fraudulent tax refund claims so far this year, protecting more than $51.2 million in state revenue.
 The department said fraudsters often use stolen personal information to file false returns and claim refunds before the real taxpayers file. “Tax fraud and identity theft remain persistent threats to state treasuries and individual taxpayers alike,” said Trish Vincent, the department’s director.
 The department said its Taxation Division does not rely only on automated rejections. Every return flagged as potentially fraudulent undergoes a manual review, in which specialists confirm the taxpayer’s identity and check the legitimacy of the refund claim before any money is released. The department said the process is meant to avoid delaying legitimate refunds.
 Taxpayers who receive a notice from the department asking for more information to verify their return should respond promptly so their refunds can be processed without unnecessary delay, the department said.
